newsitem.title: USA: Ivax in deal to sell McGaw unit for $400 million.
newsitem.headline: Ivax in deal to sell McGaw unit for $400 million.

text.p: Ivax Corp. said Friday it agreed to sell its McGaw Inc. unit to B. Braun of America Inc., a unit of B. Braun Melsungen AG, a privately owned medical products manufacturer in Germany.
Ivax, a holding company based in Miami, said the deal was a major step in its plan to refocus on its core pharmaceutical business.
It said B. Braun will pay approximately $320 million in cash at closing, subject to post-closing adjustments.

Over a period of years, which was not specified, B. Braun will make additional payments of up to $80 million, depending on the combined operating results of McGaw and B. Braun's main U.S. operating subsidiary, B. Braun Medical Inc., it said.

Ivax said it will also receive royalties and other payments based on McGaw's and B. Braun's commercialization of the Duplex drug delivery system, which is under development, Duplex is an intravenous drug delivery system designed for intravenous drugs that have limited stability after mixing.
McGaw, which is based in Irvine, Calif., makes intravenous solutions and related products. It had net revenues of $343 million and operating income of $23 million in 1996, IVAX said.
B. Braun of America, based in Bethlehem, Pa., makes disposable medical products for hospitals and other markets.
Ivax said it expects the deal to close in June.
